name: Environment Development and Society
description: The course introduces key sociological and political ecology approaches to the relationship between environment, development, and society. It examines industrialization, risk, sustainable development, resource dependence, social ecology, religion and environmental worldviews, indigenous knowledge, environmental movements, development-induced conflicts, environmental disasters, climate change, climate justice, and gender. The course also engages with the historical and conceptual debates around the Anthropocene, Capitalocene, degrowth, ecological justice, and climate coloniality, with emphasis on Indian and global case studies.Undergraduate students
